subject: Hosted API pricing: per-token horizon stepdown counterproposal
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlasai.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@atlasai.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API pricing: per-token proposal + clarifying asks

Karthik —

Thanks for the call yesterday. We reviewed Redwood's baseline per-token ladder and have a few clarifying requests before we return a formal redline. High level: Atlas AI is targeting a predictable effective rate for our hosted API usage, but we also want upside protection if burst months happen. We attached our 12-month forecast to give you a sense of volume shape.

Primary questions:
1) Can you confirm how Redwood invoices when a ladder is "marginal" vs "blended"? Concrete sample invoice lines would be helpful (we provided two month examples in the attached XLSX).
2) Does Redwood support a corridor/true-up mechanism (monthly lookback) or is reconciliation quarterly? We prefer monthly true-up given our seasonal spikes.
3) Are there performance credits available if Redwood misses the committed latency SLOs for high-priority routes?
4) Any clawback or negative true-up terms we should watch for if actuals fall below commit? We want to avoid punitive downside but understand minimum guarantees.

We're leaning toward a 6–9 month pilot with a moderate committed token floor and either a blended floor or a smooth stepdown to marginal pricing. Open to Redwood proposing a hybrid structure.

Attachments: Atlas_AI_Monthly_Forecast.xlsx (xls/x)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call this week.

—Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Platform Partnerships, Atlas AI
priya.shah@atlasai.com
+1 415-555-0182

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlasai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: per-token proposal + clarifying asks

Priya —

Appreciate the forecast; that helped a lot. Below is a concrete counterproposal and practical examples so your finance and procurement teams can model it side-by-side. Summaries first, examples after.

Summary (proposal):
- Term: 9 months pilot (Dec 2026 — Aug 2027) with a minimum monthly commit of 150M tokens.
- Pricing shape: Hybrid stepdown — blended floor for the first 3 months, then marginal ladder for months 4–9.
- True-up cadence: Monthly lookback with a 30-day invoice adjustment window.
- Performance credits: 5% monthly credit applied to invoice if 99.5% latency SLO (p95) not met on prod route (high-priority).
- Downside protection: No clawback below commit for pilot months; standard minimum guarantee applies after pilot (we can include a soft-guard for the auto-renew).

Why this structure: it gives Atlas predictability during early ramp (blended floor), then aligns unit economics to usage as you stabilize (marginal ladder) while keeping short monthly reconciliation you requested.

Concrete math (example months):
- Month A (ramp): Actual usage = 160M tokens; committed = 150M; blended floor = $0.0085/token up to commit. Invoice: 150M * $0.0085 = $1,275,000; overage 10M billed at blended overage rate $0.0078 = $78,000; total = $1,353,000.
- Month B (post-floor): Ladder (marginal) tiers: 0–150M $0.0088, 150–500M $0.0069, 500M+ $0.0058. If usage = 400M: invoice = (150M * $0.0088) + (250M * $0.0069) = $1,320,000 + $1,725,000 = $3,045,000. Effective blended rate = $0.0076125/token.

Billing notes: marginal ladder bills each incremental tier at its rate; blended floor months we apply the blended floor up to the committed volume to provide budget certainty. Monthly true-up means any over/under compared to commit is reconciled on the next invoice cycle; we can shift to a 30-day net adjustment if procurement prefers separate credits rather than line-item true-ups.

Attachments: sample invoice calc (inline) and a short term sheet draft I can send to legal.

Next steps: if Atlas is comfortable with these principals, Ben (cc'd) can draft a short pilot term sheet and I can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with your procurement and finance teams.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Office: +1 650-555-0123

From: Atlas AI Procurement <procurement@atlasai.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlasai.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: per-token proposal + clarifying asks

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear proposal. A couple quick clarifications from procurement:

- Atlas favors an effective blended guarantee for cash flow planning. We are open to a transitional blended floor but would ask that your ladder's published marginal rates are used to compute any credits so we can reconcile expected vs actual easily.
- Pilot length: we prefer 6 months with the option to extend to 9 based on consumption thresholds.
- True-up: monthly is acceptable; please include a sample invoice row with "true-up credit" and how it would display on a single-month invoice.

I've attached a lightly redlined commercial excerpt (Atlas_Redline_v2.docx) showing our ask on renewal language and minimum guarantee limits. Please review and confirm whether Redwood legal is comfortable with a no-clawback clause during the pilot.

If we can get alignment on pilot length and the blended floor math, procurement will greenlight a POC signature and move to DocuSign.

Regards,
Procurement Team
Atlas AI
procurement@atlasai.com

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Atlas AI Procurement <procurement@atlasai.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlasai.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 17 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: per-token proposal + clarifying asks

Team —

Appreciate the redline and the preference for a blended guarantee. We're willing to meet you at 6 months pilot with these refinements:

1) Pilot term: 6 months with option to auto-extend 3 months if average monthly tokens >= 250M during months 4–6.
2) Blended floor: Months 1–2 blended floor at $0.0084/token up to commit (150M). Month 3: taper to blended floor at $0.0080 up to commit. Months 4–6: marginal ladder as previously outlined.
3) No clawback for pilot: Redwood agrees to no negative clawbacks during pilot; we will not invoice retroactive penalties if Atlas falls below commit in pilot months. Standard minimum guarantee language will apply after the pilot unless otherwise renegotiated.
4) True-up: will appear on next invoice as a separate "Monthly True-Up" line with positive or negative amount; we will also provide an exportable CSV for your finance system.

I've uploaded a sample invoice PDF and the proposed short pilot term sheet to the HubSpot deal (links above). Ben will shepherd legal redlines; Prioym is on copy for implementation questions (routing, SLO measurement).

If that sounds acceptable, can someone from Atlas confirm by EOD Monday and we'll circulate a DocuSign for signature. Happy to run a 30-minute walkthrough to show the invoice mock.

–Karthik
